tool_input.body:
Closes `ethos-bfml`, `ethos-hy40`, `ethos-kcbv`, `ethos-e05k`, `ethos-jw1z` — cluster 3 of the bug triage.

## The bug

`ethos doctor` is what an operator runs to learn whether their install is sound. On a repo with **no git hooks at all**, it printed three greens:

```
Audit seal hook       PASS  not enabled here
Seal hook currency    PASS  no Seal hook section installed
Trailer hook currency PASS  no Trailer hook section installed
```

No individual check was wrong. `CheckHookCurrency` PASSing on an absent section is deliberate and documented — a dormant repo must not be told its absent hooks are stale. The defect was the **aggregate**: three checks each answering their narrow question truthfully, composing into a healthy-looking install.

Two of the five beads turned out to be one defect. `ethos-hy40`'s filed premise ("doctor checks only the seal hook") was already false; the real gap it named was **presence vs currency** — seal presence was verified when enabled, trailer presence never was, and nothing composed "enabled *and* missing" into a failure.

## What changed

**Detection is now by execution, not by pattern-matching text.** The seal detector was a lexical scan of shell source that had needed four documented patch rounds across two branches, each closing one input shape before the next review found another. A stop-loss was declared during v4.1.1: the next lexical corner converts it. That corner arrived. `hookInvocationObserved` runs the installed hook in a sandbox with a stub `ethos` on `PATH` and observes whether it was actually invoked.

**A new trailer-hook presence check** closes the `bfml`/`hy40` gap. `CheckHookCurrency` is byte-identical — verified — and the two compose without contradicting on any of the four input states.

**Two more checks**: deployed archetypes missing `require_delegated_worker` (the invariant is data-driven, so upgrading the binary without re-seeding silently yielded zero enforcement), and orphaned agent files now classified as *stale* versus *unresolved* so the detail says what to do rather than naming a symptom.

`RunAll` goes 12 → 14 checks.

## Review: 4 reviewers, 20+ findings, 3 critical

Local review ran the three seeded agents plus a security pass. Every finding was reproduced against the branch, not reasoned from prose.

**A proven sandbox escape.** `git init` inherited the caller's environment while every other command was sanitized, and its exit code was the only success proof. With `GIT_DIR` set — which `git submodule foreach` exports — `init` returned 0, created nothing, and the hook's `rev-parse` resolved to the **real repo**. `TMPDIR` points inside the repo per this org's own standard, so the "sandbox" was created in the live work tree. The check returned `observed=true`: it *passed* while the hook escaped.

The fix does not enumerate dangerous variables. The environment is allowlisted, and a **containment self-test** makes git confirm the sandbox is a sandbox before the hook runs. Measured against the buggy code with nothing else changed, the self-test caught both silent vectors without knowing either existed — including a config-injection vector nobody had named.

**"The process never started" and "the process ran and didn't call ethos" were the same value.** A CRLF hook — `core.autocrlf`, or edited on Windows — classifies as shell, fails to exec, and was reported "stale" with no error. Live on Linux, not a Windows note. Now three distinct failure messages.

**`ethos doctor` wrote to identity files.** The orphan check called a loader that triggers a voice-key migration and re-saves the YAML. A read-only diagnostic mutating the data it inspects.

**The archetype list was `ethos-e05k` again.** Hardcoded `{"implement", "test"}`, correct only by coincidence; a third seeded archetype would silently stop being monitored. Now derived from the seed embed.

**And the timeout killed a process, not a process group** — backgrounded children outlived both the timeout and the cleanup.

## Verification

Every behavioural change has a regression test **confirmed failing against pre-fix code**, pasted in its commit message. The headline regression was verified by reverting the fix and watching the test reproduce the original bug verbatim — 13/13 PASS on an enabled repo with no commit-msg hook.

`make check` green with race before each of 14 commits. `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exits 0. Detached-env gate: 28 ok, 0 FAIL.

## Phase 3

Driven through the real entry point: pre-fix and post-fix binaries built from this branch's base and tip, run against an identical fixture (enabled repo, seal hook installed, commit-msg hook removed by hand). Pre-fix showed the false PASS; post-fix showed `FAIL enabled here but no commit-msg hook`. Operator confirmation pending on this PR.

DES-077 records the decision and an explicit residual list naming what this does **not** close — sandbox-vs-reality divergence, Windows honesty rather than capability, dormant-repo trade-off, and runtime cost.

tool_input.name: bwk-doctor3
tool_input.prompt:
One review finding on PR #515 in <repo>, branch `fix/doctor-health-checks` (HEAD `cf4218b`, clean, pushed, all five CI checks green). Do NOT create or switch branches or worktrees.

**The finding, which I verified against the source before sending.** `archetypeAttemptedPath` (`internal/doctor/archetype_check.go:146-152`):

```go
repoPath := filepath.Join(repoArchRoot, "archetypes", name+".yaml")
if _, err := os.Stat(repoPath); err == nil {
    return "repo-local", repoPath
}
return "global", filepath.Join(globalRoot, "archetypes", name+".yaml")
```

Any `Stat` error falls through to "global". But `Stat` fails for reasons other than absence — EACCES on the file or on its parent directory, EIO, a symlink loop. In those cases the repo-local archetype **exists** and `LoadLayer` would have errored on it before ever reaching global, so the FAIL detail sends the operator to the wrong path to fix a file that is not the problem.

**Why this matters more than its size.** This function exists to make the archetype FAIL *actionable* — it was added because `ethos-e05k` needed to name which layer is stale. Misreporting the layer produces a detail the operator cannot act on, which is `ethos-jw1z`'s exact defect class. That is now the **third** time this cluster has reproduced the bug it was closing: the archetype check swallowed errors into a green PASS (`ethos-e05k`'s own mode), the hardcoded name list did it again, and now the remediation path does `ethos-jw1z`'s.

There is a pattern here worth naming in the fix's comment: **a fallback branch that treats "I could not determine X" as "X is the default" is the same shape as a check that treats "I could not verify" as "verified."** That is the entire subject of this branch.

**Fix:** distinguish `os.IsNotExist(err)` from every other `Stat` error. Not-exist → the repo-local file genuinely is not there, so global is the right report. Any other error → the repo-local path is what `LoadLayer` tripped on; report that path, and say the file could not be examined rather than implying it is missing.

Consider whether the returned `layer` string should carry that distinction too, since the caller renders it — "repo-local (unreadable)" is more useful than "repo-local" when the operator's next step is a `chmod` rather than an edit.

**Standards:**
- Regression test confirmed **failing against pre-fix code**, with the pre-fix output pasted. Make the repo-local archetype exist but be unstattable — a `0o000` parent directory is the portable way — and assert the reported path is the repo-local one. If that cannot be made to work as a non-root user in this test environment, say so explicitly and pin what you can instead of quietly skipping it.
- `make check` green with race before the commit. No suppressions.
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exits 0. Note the `0o000` trick behaves differently on Windows — guard or skip the test there rather than letting it fail or, worse, pass vacuously.
- Detached gate; report both the `ok` and `FAIL` counts.
- Commit. **Do not push; I push.**
- No CHANGELOG entry needed unless you judge the detail-text change user-visible enough to warrant one — say which you chose and why.

**Before committing, state what your fix makes worse, if anything.** If the answer is "nothing", say what you checked.

If the finding is wrong, say so with evidence and stop. Report when done.

tool_input.message:
No divergence to dig into. Stand down on that — you're right, and I already confirmed it independently before your message arrived.

What happened is a timing artifact of async messaging, and the fault is mine for not saying which commit I checked:

- I inspected the branch at **`9c01771`** and found S1, N1, P2, S4, N3 genuinely absent. That was accurate *at that commit*.
- You then did the work — `da61721` through `8073f83`.
- I re-verified at that point and found all of them present: `initCmd.Env`, the `SamePath` containment self-test, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, `s.Exists(handle)`, `Setpgid`/`Kill(-pid)`, `codeArchetypeNames` reading `seed.Archetypes`, and both `procgroup_unix.go` and `procgroup_windows.go`.
- The branch is pushed at **`cf4218b`**, which is `8073f83` plus one commit committing the mission contract and delegation artifacts. I confirmed `8073f83` is an ancestor.

So my "five batches not started" message was **stale by the time it reached you, not wrong when I wrote it**. Had I written "verified absent at 9c01771" instead of "still open," you'd have known immediately it was superseded. I'll pin the commit in future status claims — the same discipline I asked of you about naming which batch a report covers, and I should have been holding myself to it in the same breath.

Your correction was the right move regardless. A worker that accepts "you didn't do the work" when it demonstrably did is worse than one that pushes back with line numbers, and you brought line numbers and commit SHAs rather than assertions. That's exactly how to answer it.

**Current state:** PR #515 is open, all five CI checks green, Bugbot still running. One new review finding arrived after your work — `archetypeAttemptedPath` misreports the layer when the repo-local file exists but cannot be statted (permissions rather than absence), so the FAIL detail sends the operator to the wrong path. Already dispatched to another worker, so nothing further needed from you on it.

Worth noting for the record, since you built the thing it lands in: that finding is this cluster's signature defect for the third time. A fallback branch treating "I could not determine which layer" as "it must be global" is the same shape as a check treating "I could not verify" as "verified." The archetype check did it via the error swallow, the hardcoded list did it again, and the remediation path does it once more. Three instances inside the code written to eliminate exactly that.

Nothing else needed from you. Good work on the batch — the containment self-test in particular is the right shape, because it makes the vector enumeration's completeness irrelevant.
